question: Why can even a small tumour inside the heart cause big trouble?

options.A: The heart muscle cannot heal after a tumour forms
options.B: Cardiac tumours always release toxic chemicals into the blood
options.C: The heart is a constantly moving organ that pumps blood
options.D: Cardiac tumours prevent the lungs from breathing oxygen

explanation: Think about it like a busy pump in a tight space! Because the heart beats continuously, any extra growth inside its chambers gets in the way of normal blood flow. You've got this!

question: What part of the health record typically makes up the largest share of daily clinical data inputs?

options.A: Information technology system logs
options.B: Hospital administrative billing codes
options.C: Pharmacy inventory purchase orders
options.D: Nursing documentation and observations

explanation: Nurses constantly input vital signs, assessment notes, and care updates throughout their shifts, making up the bulk of clinical data. [learn more](GNS113_U2_T4#GNS113_U2_T4_h2)

question: An elderly patient loses sensation in their feet due to nerve issues. Which systems must they rely on most to stay balanced?

options.A: Cutaneous touch receptors
options.B: Vestibular and visual systems
options.C: Proprioceptive joint sensors
options.D: Chemical blood pressure sensors

explanation: When the feet can't feel the ground well, the patient has to depend heavily on their inner ears and eyesight to stay steady. Good clinical thinking! [learn more](GNS211_U4_T8#GNS211_U4_T8_h7)

question: What is the main reason we use a t-test in nursing research?

options.A: To measure the blood pressure of patients
options.B: To compare the averages of two groups
options.C: To calculate the total sample size needed
options.D: To observe patient behavior in a clinic

explanation: Think of a t-test as a simple way to check if the average score of one group is genuinely different from another group. You've got this!

question: What is the big win of using laparoscopy instead of traditional open surgery?

options.A: General anesthesia is never required during laparoscopic pelvic procedures
options.B: It provides a clear view of internal organs without needing any camera lights
options.C: Smaller incisions lead to faster physical recovery and less postoperative pain
options.D: Patients can leave the hospital immediately before the procedure even finishes

explanation: Correct! Tiny puncture holes mean less body trauma, quicker healing, and way less pain for the patient.

question: What is the standard first-line treatment given to pregnant women with iron deficiency anaemia?

options.A: High-dose intravenous antibiotics
options.B: Routine whole blood transfusions
options.C: Oral iron supplements
options.D: Intramuscular vitamin B12 injections

explanation: Simple and effective! Oral iron tablets are the go-to first step in antenatal clinics to help build back the mother's iron stores safely.

question: What is an immunization defaulter?

options.A: A child who misses a scheduled vaccine dose
options.B: A parent who refuses all medical treatments
options.C: A health worker who forgets to order vaccines
options.D: An infant who experiences a mild vaccine reaction

explanation: A defaulter simply refers to a child who fails to show up for a scheduled vaccine or misses a dose needed to complete their immunization schedule. [learn more](GNS214_U1_T74#GNS214_U1_T74_h1)

question: What is the very first piece of PPE a nurse should put on when donning for isolation care?

options.A: The gloves
options.B: The gown
options.C: The face mask
options.D: The eye goggles

explanation: Donning starts from the body outward, putting on the gown first so that other items like gloves can overlap the cuffs. [learn more](GST114_U2_T17#GST114_U2_T17_h5)

question: Which of these is a very common physical hazard you might find in a patient's home?

options.A: Standardized hospital call bells in every room
options.B: Sterile, bolted-down medical furniture
options.C: Continuous negative pressure isolation airflow
options.D: Frayed electrical cords and loose throw rugs

explanation: Everyday household items like loose rugs and damaged cords are top culprits for trips and falls in residential settings. Always watch out for them!

question: As a nurse examining a patient with FGM, which action should you actively avoid?

options.A: Providing a trauma-informed referral for mental health
options.B: Expressing shock, disgust, or judgment about the procedure
options.C: Screening for chronic pain and urinary symptoms
options.D: Asking for consent before performing a physical examination

explanation: Spot on! Showing negative emotions or judgment will instantly push the patient away and make them close up, ruining your therapeutic relationship.

question: Why is drying a newborn immediately after birth so crucial?

options.A: It washes away skin oils
options.B: It lowers their heart rate to normal
options.C: It stimulates breathing and keeps them warm
options.D: It stops baby jaundice from developing

explanation: Drying wipes away wet fluid so the baby doesn't get chilled from evaporation, and the rubbing action acts as a gentle nudge telling them to breathe!

question: Which complication happens when high ventilator pressures cause tiny air sacs to rupture and air leaks into the chest cavity?

options.A: Pulmonary edema
options.B: Atelectasis
options.C: Pneumothorax
options.D: Pleural effusion

explanation: Too much pressure can pop overstretched alveoli, letting air leak into the space around the lung and causing it to collapse (a pneumothorax).

question: Which lab test is a key indicator that cells are lacking oxygen and relying on backup energy pathways?

options.A: Blood lactate level
options.B: Serum sodium level
options.C: Total serum protein
options.D: Platelet count

explanation: Lactate builds up like exhaust smoke when cells are starved of oxygen and forced into anaerobic metabolism. Checking blood lactate is a quick way to see how severe the tissue oxygen shortage is.

question: Which of these is a duty of nursing management rather than leadership?

options.A: Challenging outdated hospital traditions to improve care
options.B: Mentoring junior staff to find their professional purpose
options.C: Inspiring colleagues to embrace a new clinical vision
options.D: Creating staff shift schedules and managing budgets

explanation: Spot on! Management focuses on the day-to-day operations like rotas and resources, while leadership focuses on inspiration and big-picture vision.

question: Why is it dangerous for a patient to rub their eye right after getting a numbing (anesthetic) drop?

options.A: Rubbing forces the medication deep into the tear ducts
options.B: Friction triggers an immediate severe allergy
options.C: Pressure changes will rupture internal blood vessels
options.D: They can scratch their cornea without feeling the pain

explanation: Numbing drops take away pain sensation temporarily. If the patient rubs their eye hard, they could easily scratch the delicate tissue and won't even feel it happening!

question: Which nutrient intake value is set high enough to cover almost all healthy people?

options.A: Estimated Energy Requirement (EER)
options.B: Recommended Dietary Allowance (RDA)
options.C: Estimated Average Requirement (EAR)
options.D: Tolerable Upper Intake Level (UL)

explanation: You're doing great! The RDA is set high up to make sure it meets the nutritional needs of about 97 to 98 percent of healthy folks.

question: What is a common sign that a female patient has too much androgen in her system?

options.A: Permanent drop in core body temperature
options.B: Excessive facial hair growth and acne
options.C: Extreme softening of the fingernails
options.D: Sudden loss of all body hair

explanation: High androgens stimulate oil glands and hair follicles, which frequently leads to breakouts and unexpected hair growth patterns.

question: Which research design is best for answering 'Why or how does this event happen?'

options.A: Explanatory design
options.B: Descriptive design
options.C: Historical design
options.D: Exploratory design

explanation: Brilliant! Explanatory research is built specifically to uncover the 'why' and 'how' behind health events.

question: What are the main hormonal signs that point toward Polycystic Ovary Syndrome (PCOS)?

options.A: Complete absence of estrogen production
options.B: Permanent closure of the cervical os
options.C: Hyperactivity of the thyroid gland
options.D: Androgen excess and ovulatory dysfunction

explanation: Spot on! PCOS usually brings higher levels of male hormones along with unpredictable or missing ovulation cycles. You are learning clinical concepts like a pro!

question: During which stages of pregnancy do women usually need an extra 340 to 450 calories every day?

options.A: The first two weeks after conception
options.B: First trimester only
options.C: During labor and delivery
options.D: Second and third trimesters

explanation: As that little baby starts growing super fast in the later months, the mother needs a small energy boost of extra daily calories!

question: What is the main job of anthelminthic medications?

options.A: To replace lost red blood cells
options.B: To lower elevated systemic blood pressure
options.C: To kill or expel parasitic worms
options.D: To prevent bacterial wound infections

explanation: You've got this! Anthelminthics are simply the specific drugs we use to clear parasitic worm infections from the body.

question: Which of the following tasks is classified as an Activity of Daily Living?

options.A: Banking
options.B: Bathing
options.C: Cooking
options.D: Shopping

explanation: Activities of Daily Living are basic self-care tasks required for personal independence, which include bathing, dressing, eating, and toileting. [learn more](GNS324_U3_T6#GNS324_U3_T6_h4)

question: What is an obsession in someone dealing with obsessive-compulsive neurosis?

options.A: A physical movement done to relieve muscle tension
options.B: An intrusive and unwanted thought that causes anxiety
options.C: A sudden memory loss regarding personal identity
options.D: A complete loss of contact with external reality

explanation: Spot on! Think of an obsession as an unwelcome thought or image that keeps popping into the mind against the person's will, bringing along a lot of stress.

question: If you absolutely must recap a used needle, what is the safest technique to use?

options.A: The one-handed scoop technique
options.B: Holding the cap tightly in the palm of your hand
options.C: Pushing the needle directly into the cap using both hands
options.D: Asking a colleague to hold the cap while you insert the needle

explanation: Brilliant! The one-handed scoop method keeps your free hand safely away from the sharp tip so you don't accidentally poke yourself. [learn more](GNS122_U4_T2#GNS122_U4_T2_h7)

question: What is the primary symptom that distinguishes extravasation from simple fluid infiltration?

options.A: Severe blistering, tissue damage, or necrosis
options.B: A slight slowing of the gravity drip rate
options.C: Sudden cooling of the surrounding skin area
options.D: Leaking of clear fluid around the adhesive tape

explanation: Extravasation happens with vesicant drugs that destroy local tissue, whereas simple infiltration involves non-harmful fluids. [learn more](GNS122_U1_T4#GNS122_U1_T4_h8)

question: What does 'market equilibrium' mean in simple terms?

options.A: Consumers buy everything available without worrying about their budgets
options.B: The quantity demanded by consumers equals the quantity supplied by producers
options.C: The government sets a fixed price for all goods sold in the country
options.D: Producers make maximum profit by charging the highest possible prices

explanation: Equilibrium is the sweet spot where what buyers want matches exactly what sellers are putting out. Everything balances out! [learn more](GST322_U1_T1#GST322_U1_T1_h5)

question: How does an autoclave sterilize infectious waste?

options.A: By freezing the waste to extremely low temperatures
options.B: By soaking the waste in strong liquid bleach
options.C: By using high-pressure steam to kill pathogens
options.D: By crushing the waste into tiny metal cubes

explanation: Autoclaves use heat, moisture, and high pressure to destroy infectious microorganisms effectively before disposal. [learn more](GST114_U6_T12#GST114_U6_T12_h7)

question: What is a major reason why Nigeria is facing a shortage of skilled nurses right now?

options.A: A complete ban on private nursing practice
options.B: The mass migration of healthcare professionals abroad
options.C: Mandatory retirement at age thirty
options.D: The total closure of all nursing training institutions

explanation: Spot on. Many skilled nurses are travelling abroad for better opportunities, leaving a big gap at home.

question: Why should community health nurses plan health programs *with* the people rather than just *for* them?

options.A: It guarantees that government funding will double instantly
options.B: It completely removes the need to write nursing reports
options.C: It ensures programs respect local culture and gain community support
options.D: It allows the nurse to skip doing fieldwork entirely

explanation: Great thinking! When community members are involved from the start, they trust the process more and the program actually fits their daily lives.

question: An infant is brought to the clinic at 14 weeks old with no previous shots. What should you do?

options.A: Tell the mother to return when the child reaches one year of age
options.B: Wait until the child is two years old before starting any injections
options.C: Administer catch-up doses according to the national guidelines
options.D: Give only the birth vaccines since the infant missed the early schedule

explanation: Don't worry if a baby comes in late! Just use national catch-up guidelines to get them protected as safely and quickly as possible.

question: What should you do if a confused patient repeatedly refuses to be turned to their side?

options.A: Tell the patient they will be discharged if they do not comply
options.B: Document the refusal, explain the risks, and notify the primary nurse or provider
options.C: Document that the patient is sleeping and skip all future turns
options.D: Ignore the refusal and hold the patient down forcibly

explanation: Patients have a right to refuse, but as their nurse, you must gently educate them on the risks and report it properly.

question: When should a nurse put on a disposable gown and gloves for contact precautions?

options.A: Immediately before leaving the isolation ward
options.B: Before entering the patient's room or care area
options.C: Only when performing open wound dressing changes
options.D: After touching contaminated hospital bed rails

explanation: Always gown and glove up *before* stepping into the room. That way, your clothes and hands stay clean right from the start.

question: How should a nurse handle a competent patient who refuses a necessary home treatment?

options.A: Respect their autonomy while explaining the risks and documenting the refusal
options.B: Discontinue all future nursing visits without notifying the doctor
options.C: Call the police to have the patient admitted to a hospital ward
options.D: Force the treatment immediately to avoid future legal trouble

explanation: Competent adults have the right to make decisions about their bodies, provided they understand the consequences of refusing care. [learn more](GNS324_U1_T11#GNS324_U1_T11_h7)

question: Which of these is NOT a typical limitation of questionnaire-based studies?

options.A: The potential for respondents to misunderstand written items
options.B: The lack of opportunity to ask follow-up probing questions
options.C: The ability to immediately observe complex clinical healing processes
options.D: The risk of receiving very low response rates from participants

explanation: Questionnaires collect self-reported written data; they do not allow a nurse to physically observe clinical healing processes firsthand. You are crushing these questions!

question: What is the term used to describe the social, economic, and environmental factors that shape mental wellbeing?

options.A: Clinical diagnostic criteria
options.B: Biological stress markers
options.C: Social determinants of health
options.D: Hereditary personality traits

explanation: Social determinants of health encompass the conditions in which people are born, grow, live, work, and age that heavily influence mental health. [learn more](GNS314_U1_T7#GNS314_U1_T7_h2)

question: When dressing a stroke patient with weakness on one side, where should you put the clothes first?

options.A: Whichever side they prefer
options.B: The strong or unaffected side
options.C: Both sides at the exact same time
options.D: The weak or affected side

explanation: Brilliant! Dressing the weak side first saves the patient from painful, awkward twisting of a limb that lacks strength.

question: Which sign is a clinical indicator of severe respiratory distress in an adult patient?

options.A: Relaxed posture in a flat bed
options.B: Slow and deep regular breathing
options.C: Use of accessory neck muscles
options.D: Warm and pink skin coloration

explanation: When breathing becomes very hard, patients use their neck and chest muscles to help force air in and out. [learn more](GNS315_U2_T2#GNS315_U2_T2_h3)

question: A patient keeps coming back to the hospital, and you notice relatives arguing loudly at the bedside. How would Family Systems Theory explain this?

options.A: The family tension at home is slowing down the patient's recovery
options.B: The patient is ignoring medication just to annoy people
options.C: The doctors failed to find the main physical illness
options.D: The hospital building is the only reason they are arguing

explanation: Stress at home gets under a patient's skin! Unresolved arguments and family tension can genuinely hold back physical healing.

question: Why is it so important for the immune system to tell the difference between 'self' and 'non-self'?

options.A: It prevents the immune system from attacking healthy host tissues
options.B: It ensures that nutrients are absorbed properly in the intestines
options.C: It helps the body maintain a stable internal core temperature
options.D: It allows red blood cells to carry more oxygen to organs

explanation: Knowing what belongs to the body ('self') stops the immune system from mistakenly attacking healthy organs and tissues—which is what happens in autoimmune diseases!

question: Why might a patient with high blood cell counts paradoxically face bleeding risks?

options.A: The body stops making fibrinogen completely
options.B: The excess platelets do not function right
options.C: Phlebotomy removes all clotting proteins
options.D: High blood pressure bursts skin capillaries

explanation: Even though platelet numbers look high, they are often faulty and don't do their clotting job properly, leading to bleeding worries.

question: What is the primary goal of occupational health hazard control?

options.A: To reduce the cost of buying new equipment
options.B: To punish workers who break safety rules
options.C: To treat workers only after an accident occurs
options.D: To prevent injuries and illnesses before they happen

explanation: Hazard control focuses on stopping workplace dangers from causing harm in the first place rather than just dealing with the aftermath. [learn more](GNS225_U7_T8#GNS225_U7_T8_h1)

question: Which of the following is NOT a typical outcome of a toxic or poor leadership style in nursing?

options.A: Increased nurse absenteeism
options.B: Communication breakdowns
options.C: Improved patient safety culture
options.D: High staff burnout rates

explanation: Poor leadership damages safety culture rather than improving it, leading to errors and poor teamwork. [learn more](GST321_U3_T3#GST321_U3_T3_h7)

question: Why is early contraceptive counseling crucial immediately following abortion treatment?

options.A: Because hormonal contraceptives immediately cure any underlying uterine infections
options.B: Because ovulation can return as early as two weeks after an abortion
options.C: Because federal law mandates contraceptive use before hospital discharge
options.D: Because patients lose their fertility permanently if they wait one month

explanation: That's right! A woman can get pregnant again very quickly, even before her first normal period returns, making immediate counseling essential.

question: What is the ultimate, primary benefit of using healthcare simulation in nursing education?

options.A: Eliminating the need for written exams and classroom lectures

options.C: Improving patient safety and reducing medical errors in hospitals
options.D: Reducing the cost of running nursing schools and hiring staff

explanation: Every simulation exercise is ultimately aimed at protecting real patients by ensuring nurses are well-trained and competent. [learn more](GNS212_U4_T8#GNS212_U4_T8_h6)

question: What must a nurse do before changing how they care for patients based on a new research paper?

options.A: Carefully check the study's validity and methods first
options.B: Wait ten whole years before taking any action
options.C: Just assume it's true because it was printed in a magazine
options.D: Ask every single hospital patient for their permission

explanation: Evidence-based practice means we don't just follow every new trend blindly; we appraise the research to make sure it's solid and safe.

question: Which sensory receptors deep in the skin are great at detecting deep pressure and heavy vibrations?

options.A: Pacinian corpuscles
options.B: Free nerve endings
options.C: Meissner corpuscles
options.D: Merkel discs

explanation: Spot on! Pacinian corpuscles are shaped like tiny onions and sit deep in the skin to sense firm pressure and vibrations.

question: Why is the home-based child health card such a lifesaver in immunization programs?

options.A: It automatically orders new vaccine supplies from the central store
options.B: It replaces the need for nurses to keep facility registers
options.C: It acts as a legal permit for children to enter primary school
options.D: It provides a portable, lifelong record that travels with the child

explanation: Parents keep it safe at home and bring it along, meaning any nurse anywhere can instantly see what vaccines the child has received!

question: Why do doctors treat tuberculosis (TB) with a mix of several drugs instead of just one?

options.A: To eliminate the need for routine liver function tests
options.B: To prevent the development of drug-resistant strains
options.C: To speed up the patient discharge process immediately
options.D: To reduce the financial cost of purchasing drugs

explanation: TB bacteria are clever and mutate easily. Hitting them with multiple drugs at once makes it much harder for them to fight back and become resistant.

question: You are about to give a patient a drug with a dosage you aren't sure about. What should you do?

options.A: Check the formulary or drug guide to confirm the correct safe dosage range
options.B: Administer the medication immediately to avoid delaying ward routines
options.C: Throw the medication away in the clinical waste bin without telling anyone
options.D: Ask another patient in the same ward what dose they usually take

explanation: Always double-check! Consulting a trusted drug guide keeps your patient safe and builds your clinical confidence.

question: How many unique patient identifiers must a nurse check before giving any medication?

options.A: Zero identifiers
options.B: Two identifiers
options.C: One identifier
options.D: Four identifiers

explanation: Checking two unique identifiers, such as the patient's full name and hospital number, ensures the medicine goes to the right person. [learn more](GNS112_U4_T7#GNS112_U4_T7_h5)

question: How does keeping a patient close to your body help protect your back during a transfer?

options.A: It reduces the physical load and leverage on your spine
options.B: It makes the patient feel much safer and calmer
options.C: It prevents the patient from falling forward
options.D: It allows you to finish the hospital shift faster

explanation: Keeping heavy objects close to your center of gravity decreases the strain placed on your lower back muscles. [learn more](GNS222_U1_T25#GNS222_U1_T25_h3)

question: Which facial nerve problem puts a leprosy patient at risk of going blind?

options.A: Bell's palsy
options.B: Lagophthalmos
options.C: Jaw nerve pain
options.D: Facial drooping

question: Which everyday nursing action relies most directly on the discovery of germ theory?

options.A: Helping the patient perform passive range of motion exercises
options.B: Performing strict hand hygiene and surgical asepsis
options.C: Documenting vital signs every four hours on the bedside chart
options.D: Assessing the patient's nutritional status and dietary intake

explanation: Handwashing and sterile techniques are our frontline defense to stop germs from spreading between patients. Pure nursing basics!

question: What is the primary tool nurses use to map out a family health history across generations?

options.A: A Punnett square
options.B: A blood glucose log
options.C: A genogram
options.D: A karyotype chart

explanation: A genogram is a visual family tree that helps nurses map inherited diseases and health patterns across generations. [learn more](GNS111_U1_T7#GNS111_U1_T7_h7)

question: What is the main purpose of emergency obstetric care networks?

options.A: To replace the need for routine antenatal checkups
options.B: To reduce the overall birth rate in rural populations
options.C: To provide long-term family planning counseling
options.D: To treat sudden, life-threatening complications during birth

explanation: Correct! These networks ensure that when a sudden crisis hits during labor, mothers can get life-saving emergency care fast.

question: A patient has sudden flare-ups of numbness and weakness that completely clear up after a few weeks, followed by long periods of normal health. What pattern is this?

options.A: Secondary progressive
options.B: Relapsing-remitting
options.C: Primary progressive
options.D: Benign transient paresis

explanation: This is the classic 'relapsing-remitting' pattern—clear flare-ups (relapses) followed by periods where the patient recovers and feels fine (remissions).

question: You notice a student nurse leaning heavily on the patient's chest between chest compressions. What advice should you give?

options.A: Bend your elbows to reduce pressure on the patient's ribs
options.B: Allow full chest recoil so the heart can refill with blood
options.C: Stop compressions completely and check for a carotid pulse
options.D: Increase the speed to one hundred fifty pushes per minute

explanation: Leaning is a common mistake! Remind them to let the chest spring all the way back up so the heart chambers can refill with fresh blood for the next push.

question: What is the medical reason for performing Female Genital Mutilation (FGM)?

options.A: Enhancement of fertility during childbearing years
options.B: Reduction of congenital reproductive abnormalities
options.C: Prevention of chronic pelvic inflammatory disease
options.D: There is no medical justification for the procedure

question: What is the absolute first thing a nurse must do if a patient shows signs of neuroleptic malignant syndrome (NMS)?

options.A: Discontinue the antipsychotic medication immediately
options.B: Increase the fluid intake by mouth
options.C: Apply warm blankets to raise body temperature

question: What is the primary function of carbohydrates in the human body?

options.A: To build strong bones and teeth
options.B: To transport oxygen in the blood
options.C: To provide the body's primary and most efficient source of energy
options.D: To repair damaged skin tissue

explanation: Carbohydrates break down into glucose, which fuels the brain, organs, and muscles for daily activities. [learn more](GNS227_U1_T005#GNS227_U1_T005_h2)

question: How are health outcomes usually measured in a Cost-Effectiveness Analysis?

options.A: Natural clinical units like life-years gained or blood pressure lowered
options.B: Subjective happiness scales completely unrelated to physical health
options.C: Monetary amounts such as dollars or naira earned by the hospital
options.D: Total number of staff employed in the outpatient department

explanation: Instead of money, cost-effectiveness looks at real clinical results—like millimeters of mercury dropped in blood pressure or extra years of life gained.

question: Why is connecting a patient to community resources like vocational training important?

options.A: It forces them to work without getting any rest
options.B: It ensures the clinic makes a financial profit
options.C: It replaces the need for talking to a nurse or doctor
options.D: It helps them regain independence and purpose through meaningful activity

explanation: Community resources like job training help patients reintegrate into society and build a fulfilling life after illness. [learn more](GNS314_U4_T5#GNS314_U4_T5_h7)

question: Before physically transporting a patient for an external referral, what crucial step must the nurse or doctor complete?

options.A: Contact the receiving facility to confirm bed availability and acceptance
options.B: Ask the patient to pay all hospital bills in full cash
options.C: Throw away all previous paper records to save luggage space
options.D: Wait for the patient's extended family to arrive from another city

explanation: Checking in advance ensures the receiving hospital is ready and expecting the patient, avoiding dangerous delays in ongoing treatment. [learn more](GNS112_U2_T5#GNS112_U2_T5_h4)

question: A pregnant client at 32 weeks gestation reports a sudden severe headache and blurred vision. What is the most appropriate nursing action?

options.A: Suggest she drink more water and take a mild over-the-counter pain reliever
options.B: Notify the primary care provider immediately to evaluate for preeclampsia
options.C: Reassure her that these are normal symptoms of increased blood volume
options.D: Advise her to lie flat on her back for an hour to relieve eye strain

explanation: Severe headaches and visual disturbances are cardinal signs of gestational hypertension or preeclampsia, which require urgent medical evaluation. [learn more](GNS226_U2_T003#GNS226_U2_T003_h6)

question: When we talk about 'psychosocial' care in mental health nursing, what two main things are we bringing together?

options.A: Laboratory values and physical symptoms
options.B: Emotional experiences and environmental conditions
options.C: Surgical history and genetic mutations
options.D: Medication side effects and dietary habits

explanation: Spot on! Psychosocial care looks at both sides of the coin: what is happening inside a person's mind (psychological) and what is happening in their world outside (social).

question: What does the letter 'D' stand for in the HEADSS adolescent assessment tool?

options.A: Drugs, alcohol, and tobacco use
options.B: Depression and developmental delays
options.C: Diet, disease, and daily exercise
options.D: Discipline at school and home

question: How do many individuals with behaviour disorders view neutral, everyday actions from other people?

options.A: As deliberate threats
options.B: As acts of confusion
options.C: As friendly gestures
options.D: As signs of weakness

explanation: They often have a 'hostile attribution bias,' meaning they wrongly assume others are out to get them even when they aren't.

question: Why do we combine two different drugs in Artemisinin-Based Combination Therapy (ACT)?

options.A: To make the medication taste better for young children
options.B: To shorten the treatment duration to a single dose
options.C: To eliminate the need for any laboratory blood testing
options.D: To prevent or delay the development of parasite resistance

question: Which level of health care serves as the foundation or bedrock of the Nigerian health system?

options.A: Secondary health care
options.B: Tertiary health care
options.C: Primary health care
options.D: Private laboratory care

explanation: Primary health care is designed to be the first point of contact and the foundation of the entire health delivery system. [learn more](GST322_U5_T2#GST322_U5_T2_h2)

question: Why must a feeding tube be flushed with warm water before and after giving formula?

options.A: To check the patient's blood pressure

options.D: To cool down the internal stomach lining

question: What was the primary goal of early psychiatric asylums?

options.D: To test new pharmaceutical medications

question: What does the principle of informed choice mean for a pregnant woman?

options.A: Her family makes all healthcare decisions for her
options.B: She understands both the benefits and risks of home birth
options.C: She must choose a hospital regardless of her wishes
options.D: She can demand any medication she wants during labor

question: What common health problem can happen when cultural food taboos stop pregnant women from eating meat and eggs?

options.A: Gestational diabetes mellitus
options.B: Excessive fetal birth weight
options.C: Rapid maternal weight gain
options.D: Severe iron-deficiency anemia

question: Why is women empowerment considered essential for achieving universal health coverage?

options.B: It allows women to actively participate in seeking and utilizing healthcare services
options.C: It completely removes the financial cost of purchasing hospital drugs
options.D: It guarantees that only female doctors will treat patients

question: Why do patients with long-standing chronic pancreatitis eventually develop diabetes mellitus?

options.A: Dietary restrictions force the body to rely entirely on stored body fat.

question: Why should the person who orders hospital supplies be different from the person who approves the payment?

options.A: To ensure that nurses never have to handle administrative paperwork
options.B: To maintain separation of duties and reduce the risk of fraud
options.C: To allow the finance department to dictate clinical patient care
options.D: To make sure orders take longer to process through the system

explanation: Separating these duties creates a safety net. When two different people handle ordering and paying, it greatly reduces the chance of theft or financial mix-ups.

question: Why does the healthcare market struggle to act like a normal open market?

options.A: Doctors and hospitals never charge money for emergency life-saving procedures
options.B: The supply of doctors always matches the exact number of sick people
options.C: Government regulations, insurance systems, and emergencies constantly interfere with free market forces
options.D: Patients always know the exact cost of their medical treatments before admission

explanation: Healthcare isn't like buying shoes. Emergencies happen without warning, and governments step in because health is a basic human right, not just a commodity. [learn more](GST322_U1_T1#GST322_U1_T1_h5)

question: What hemoglobin level generally tells us an expectant mother has anaemia in her first trimester?

options.D: Below 11.0 g/dL

question: Which body part usually shows the yellow discoloration first when a baby develops jaundice?

options.A: The abdomen and thighs
options.B: The sclera and the face
options.C: The palms of the hands
options.D: The soles of the feet

explanation: Jaundice typically starts from the head and moves downward, meaning the eyes and face show the yellow color before the trunk and limbs do. [learn more](GNS226_U3_T017#GNS226_U3_T017_h1)

question: Why must broad-spectrum antibiotics be given right away to a patient with a septic incomplete abortion?

options.A: To directly stimulate uterine contractions and expel retained tissue
options.B: To control and prevent the spread of ascending bacterial infection and septic shock
options.C: To replace lost blood volume and increase hemoglobin levels

question: Which patient group requires strict fluid intake and output monitoring?

options.A: Patients taking diuretic medications
options.B: Patients waiting for outpatient eye surgery
options.C: Patients with mild, healing skin scratches
options.D: Patients admitted for routine physical exams

question: Which emergency during the third stage of labor requires an immediate hospital transfer?

options.A: Mild postpartum fatigue
options.B: Normal placental separation
options.C: Transient shivering after birth
options.D: Severe postpartum hemorrhage

explanation: Heavy bleeding after delivery can quickly become life-threatening. Stop the bleeding and get the mother to the hospital fast!

question: In the chain of infection, what do we call the cozy home base where a germ lives, grows, and multiplies?

options.A: Susceptible host
options.B: Portal of entry
options.C: Reservoir
options.D: Infectious agent

explanation: Think of a reservoir as a germ's favorite hangout spot—like a human body, an animal, or a damp surface where it can multiply!

question: What is a major health risk in overcrowded refugee or displaced persons (IDP) camps?

options.A: A sudden surplus of safe drinking water
options.B: Complete elimination of nutritional deficiencies
options.C: Immediate eradication of chronic lifestyle illnesses
options.D: Rapid outbreaks of waterborne and communicable diseases

explanation: Well done! When people live close together with poor sanitation, infections like cholera and measles can spread very quickly.

question: What is the number one thing that encourages young people to open up and share sensitive health info with a nurse?

options.A: Free mobile phones
options.B: Presence of tribal leaders
options.C: Free meals at the clinic
options.D: Guaranteed confidentiality

explanation: Trust is everything! Teens need to know their secrets are safe with you before they'll feel comfortable talking about their health.

question: A heart failure patient uses a wearable at home. Which trend should make a nurse step in early?

options.A: Gradual upward trends in daily weight and decreasing physical activity
options.B: Stable resting heart rates recorded consistently throughout the night
options.C: Occasional reminders to stand up and stretch during sedentary hours
options.D: A slight increase in daily step counts reported over the weekend

explanation: When activity drops and weight creeps up from fluid, it's often an early warning sign that heart failure symptoms are worsening.

question: A tele-nurse sees that a heart failure patient's daily weight readings are steadily climbing. What should the nurse do next?

options.A: Contact the patient to assess for worsening fluid overload symptoms
options.B: Ignore the data until the patient's next scheduled annual checkup
options.C: Advise the patient to stop taking all prescribed medications immediately
options.D: Delete the readings because home devices are always inaccurate

explanation: Quick thinking! Gaining weight fast in heart failure often means the body is holding onto extra fluid. Calling the patient lets you catch it early before they end up in the hospital.

question: Why shouldn't you give anti-bleeding (antihaemorrhagic) drugs to a patient who already has active blood clots?

options.A: It lowers their blood pressure too quickly
options.B: It stops the liver from making albumin
options.C: It prevents the kidneys from filtering urine
options.D: It can cause dangerous new clots in vital organs

explanation: If a patient is already forming unwanted clots, giving drugs that promote clotting is like pouring fuel on a fire—it can cause dangerous blockages!

question: How does the daily work of a PHC nurse differ mainly from a nurse in a high-tech hospital ICU?

options.A: The hospital nurse spends most of their time farming and digging boreholes
options.B: The PHC nurse focuses heavily on community outreach, health promotion, and preventive education
options.C: The PHC nurse is forbidden from touching patients or administering medications
options.D: The PHC nurse only provides end-of-life care and palliative treatments

explanation: Well done! While hospital nurses focus heavily on treating acute illness, PHC nurses focus on keeping the wider community well through prevention and health education.

question: Which of these is a classic example of an anthropometric measurement?

options.A: Daily water consumption

options.D: Blood pressure reading

explanation: You've got this! Anthropometric just means measuring physical body dimensions like height, weight, and BMI.

question: Why are straps fastened across the chest, hips, and knees during ambulance transport?

question: Why should you test a new idea on a small scale before launching it across the whole hospital?

options.A: It ensures that hospital management never finds out about the project
options.B: It eliminates all paperwork requirements for the nursing unit
options.C: It completely stops nurses from making any clinical errors ever again
options.D: It minimizes risk and allows staff to refine the process safely

explanation: Testing on a small scale lets you find little mistakes and fix them safely before rolling the change out to the entire hospital.

question: While looking at an ovary slide under a microscope, you spot a large fluid-filled space called an antrum. What kind of follicle is this?

options.A: Primordial follicle

options.C: Atretic follicle

question: How often should you turn an immobile patient to protect their skin from pressure sores?

options.A: At least every two hours
options.B: Every six hours
options.C: Only when the family asks
options.D: Once every shift

question: What is the main goal of selecting patients for home delivery?

options.A: Maximizing maternal and newborn safety

options.C: Promoting traditional herbs
options.D: Reducing hospital utility bills

question: What are the three main building blocks of healthcare financing?

options.A: Revenue collection, risk pooling, and purchasing
options.B: Drug manufacturing, supply, and distribution
options.C: Budgeting, staffing, and facility management
options.D: Patient admission, treatment, and discharge

explanation: Think of healthcare financing like a cooperative thrift society: you collect money, pool the risk together, and buy what the group needs. These three steps keep health systems running!

question: Why do public health campaigns often provide free childhood immunizations?

options.A: Pharmaceutical companies give away extra vaccines to charity for free
options.B: Vaccines create positive externalities by building community herd immunity
options.C: Infectious diseases never spread unless children are in school
options.D: Parents refuse to take their children to private clinics for shots

explanation: Brilliant! When you immunize a child, you don't just protect them—you shield the whole community by stopping the spread of disease. That's a powerful positive externality! [learn more](GST322_U1_T1#GST322_U1_T1_h6)

question: What is a major cause of strain on traditional family elder care systems in Nigeria?

options.A: Mandatory government placement of all seniors into nursing homes

options.C: Urbanization and the migration of younger relatives to cities
options.D: The total absence of any chronic health conditions in the elderly

question: What is the best way to make sure a family caregiver truly understands your infection control instructions?

question: What does a line that slopes upward on a healthcare chart tell you?

question: What do we mean by a "learning experience" in your nursing training?

question: What are the three core principles of radiation safety?

options.A: Time, distance, and shielding

question: How can stagnant water or soil act as a source of community infection?

options.A: By attracting human carriers to contaminated areas

options.D: By mutating human cells to create new viruses

question: What is a clear sign that an expectorant is working successfully?

question: Which of these medications is a well-known first-generation (typical) antipsychotic?

question: Which symptom is a classic warning sign of severely high blood pressure?

question: What do we call the grief family members feel *before* their loved one actually passes away?

question: In occupational health, what does a 'zoonotic disease' mean?

question: How does evidence-based nutrition mainly differ from traditional food folklore?

question: What is a key responsibility for a nurse right after a screening test is completed?

question: What is the primary goal of psychological triage during a disaster?

question: What is a very common physical change patients notice after they start eating a healthier diet?

question: What is gluten's main job when baking bread and pastries?

options.B: It preserves food against bacterial spoilage

question: Which measurements do nurses routinely track to monitor a patient's progress on a low-calorie diet?

options.A: Daily resting handgrip strength

question: Which two brain chemicals are mainly responsible for balancing excitation and inhibition?

question: How does chronic high blood pressure eventually lead to heart failure?

question: What does 'sample hemolysis' mean in the laboratory?

question: How can nurse leaders best help staff accept new policies suggested by an audit?

question: A patient is scheduled for an upper GI scope to check ongoing internal bleeding. What is the main goal?

question: How often should vital signs be monitored immediately after an MVA procedure during the first hour?

question: What does the acronym PMTCT stand for in healthcare?

options.C: Primary Medical Treatment and Care Techniques

question: Why is it so crucial that a patient stays completely still during a spine CT scan?

question: What is looked at first when choosing drugs for the Nigerian Essential Medicines List?

question: Why is a 'blameless' reporting culture so good for hospital safety?

options.C: It allows hospital management to ignore minor documentation errors

question: Why was the Minimum Data Set (MDS) introduced as part of the 1987 reforms?

options.C: To calculate the exact profit margins for private facility owners

question: Which of these is one of the most common types of errors in clinical practice?

question: Why must everyone in a household get treated at the same time if one person has pinworms?

question: You notice rising rates of malnutrition in a local village during your community posting. What is your best first step as a nurse?

question: What is the main goal of restorative nursing programs in skilled facilities?

question: When do patients most commonly move into a skilled nursing facility?

question: What is the main goal of environmental hygiene in public health?

question: Which nursing advice helps prevent burnout in a gifted child with a packed daily schedule?

question: Why is foetal scalp blood sampling sometimes performed when a CTG is abnormal?

question: Why must patients take their hormone replacement medication for life?

question: Why can deep-seated traditional beliefs sometimes cause trouble for NGO health outreaches?

question: Why must blood cultures be drawn before giving the first dose of antibiotics?

question: How does your nervous system's 'fight-or-flight' (sympathetic) response affect your intestines?

options.C: It increases digestive enzyme output

question: Why do we need a clear research problem before starting any study?

question: What happens to the body during the stage of exhaustion under long-term, chronic stress?

question: Why is it so important to use short, simple sentences when talking to an extremely anxious patient?
